description: Given an Airflow DAG's schedule_interval/default_args/max_active_runs/params/TaskGroup, author the Orchestra pipeline root: schedule (6-field cron), configuration.retries/retry_delay/timeout/concurrency, and inputs — dropping orchestrator-specific concepts (catchup, pools, depends_on_past) with an explicit flag rather than force-fitting them, and flattening nested TaskGroups into a single stage.

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG to the Orchestra pipeline root (see files/nightly_elt_dag.py) — schedule, retries, timeout, and concurrency only, don't worry about the task bodies yet. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline root with version v1, a 6-field cron schedule converted from '0 2 * * *' in UTC, configuration.retries=2, configuration.retry_delay=5 (timedelta(minutes=5)), configuration.timeout=3600 (timedelta(hours=1) in seconds), and configuration.concurrency.max_active=1 (from max_active_runs=1). The 'elt'/'nightly' tags land on every task, not the enclosing stage, and owner/depends_on_past/catchup are dropped rather than force-fit anywhere.

assertions.text: Schedule uses a 6-field AWS EventBridge cron (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week year), not Airflow's 5-field schedule_interval copied verbatim
The 'elt' and 'nightly' tags are preserved as task-level tags on every task (or noted under meta) rather than lost or placed on the enclosing stage/TaskGroupModel
owner, depends_on_past, and catchup=False are dropped without being force-fit into an unrelated field or fabricating a comment that isn't warranted

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG's pipeline root to Orchestra (see files/partner_sync_dag.py). It has no schedule — it's only triggered manually or by an upstream automation. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline root with no schedule: block (or webhook: {enabled: true} noted instead), inputs.target_env (from DAG params) and inputs.table (from Variable.get('table', default_var='orders')) mapped with their defaults, and PARTNER_API_KEY represented as a connection/${{ ENV.* }} reference rather than an input or literal value.

assertions.text: PARTNER_API_KEY is referenced (as a connection or ${{ ENV.* }}), not silently dropped
No schedule: block is invented — schedule_interval=None in the source, so the pipeline either omits schedule: or sets webhook: {enabled: true}, not a guessed cron
PARTNER_API_KEY does not become an inputs: field — it's a secret read via os.environ, so it belongs on the connection, not inputs

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG's pipeline root and task structure to Orchestra (see files/regional_backfill_dag.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline root with configuration.retries=3 and configuration.retry_delay capped at 120 (retry_delay=timedelta(hours=3)=180 minutes, over the 120-minute cap) with a flagging comment, and the nested TaskGroup structure (regional_extract > emea, apac) flattened into a single Orchestra stage containing all four tasks (extract_emea, load_emea, extract_apac, load_apac) rather than represented as three separate or nested stages. catchup=True is dropped and explicitly flagged, not silently ignored.

assertions.text: configuration.retry_delay is capped at 120 (not 180, the uncapped timedelta(hours=3) conversion)
The retry_delay cap is called out with a comment or note explaining the source value exceeded 120 minutes
All four tasks from the nested TaskGroups appear in the output

The nested TaskGroups (regional_extract containing emea and apac) are flattened into a single Orchestra stage, not represented as three separate stages or a nested/stage-within-stage structure — TaskGroupModel has no nested-stage field
catchup=True is explicitly flagged as having no Orchestra equivalent (a MANUAL/comment note), rather than silently dropped
